title: A self-sustaining, net-electric fusion power plant

concept.text: The proposed innovation is an integrated fusion power plant that sustains positive net electrical output while maintaining its equipment and fuel supply. Fusion would supply energy for conversion into electricity, with enough electrical generation to cover the facility’s own consumption and deliver a surplus. Achieving this would require fusion production, energy conversion, plant operations, maintenance and fuel management to work together over a substantial operating campaign.

The accounting boundary is fundamental. Target gain compares fusion energy with energy delivered to a fusion target. Plasma gain compares fusion power with external heating supplied to the plasma. A plant-wide electrical balance includes electricity generation and consumption across the facility. Each measure answers a different engineering question, and establishing sustained electricity production requires the whole-facility balance.

Concept synthesis. Self-sustaining operation here includes a credible continuing fuel supply and maintainable components, alongside positive electrical output. For a deuterium–tritium implementation, the proposed scope includes integrated tritium breeding and recovery sufficient to support continued operation. The concept leaves room for different fusion approaches, provided they meet the integrated operating requirements.

significance.text: If demonstrated, the direct breakthrough would be a new source of sustained net electricity from fusion. Its significance would come from closing the complete energy-production chain, including the facility’s electrical demands. Controllable operation would be an additional requirement of a practical power plant, whose operating flexibility would need demonstration.

Conditional impact synthesis. Reliable, economically manufactured fusion plants could expand electricity supply and contribute to emissions reductions where their deployment changes the generation mix. Those outcomes depend on lifecycle costs, manufacturing capacity, infrastructure, operating reliability and adoption. A successful net-electric demonstration would establish an important technical capability while leaving the scale and pace of its wider effects open.

Impact synthesis. The revolutionary step is the integrated operating capability. Target ignition and high plasma gain can supply enabling evidence, while maintainability, continued fuel availability and practical electricity production determine whether that progress becomes a durable power source. Competitive economics and successful replication would require evidence beyond the first qualifying plant.

missing_breakthrough.text: The capability to establish is sustained positive electrical output from the complete facility. Fusion performance must support energy conversion and every electrical demand within the chosen plant boundary. The engineering challenge is therefore to combine sufficiently productive fusion with an electrical system whose generation exceeds total consumption across actual operating cycles.

Engineering synthesis. Productive fusion must also be compatible with component lifetimes, maintenance procedures and sufficient operating availability. Equipment replacement, recovery from interruptions and the energy used during startup and shutdown all affect the integrated result. The supplied evidence does not quantify the remaining performance gaps or establish which subsystem currently limits each fusion approach.

Candidate engineering questions retained with qualification. For deuterium–tritium designs, managing neutron exposure and breeding and recovering tritium are proposed central challenges. Convincing resolution would require components that remain serviceable under the intended conditions and a fuel system that supplies usable tritium at the rate continued operation requires. The supplied sources do not substantiate the severity or present status of these challenges, so their ranking and distance from resolution remain open.

Evidence-bounded synthesis. The supplied material establishes important differences between experimental fusion gain and facility-wide electrical gain. It leaves the worldwide status of the complete integrated capability unresolved as of November 1, 2026. The remaining breakthrough is defined here by the capability to demonstrate, with no global absence claim inferred from the limitations of the two facilities described.

current_state.text: According to the LLNL milestone passage documented in the supplied review, the National Ignition Facility’s June 20, 2026 shot produced 7.9 MJ of fusion energy, with a measurement uncertainty of ±0.4 MJ and target gain of approximately 3.8. The gain denominator was laser energy delivered to the target. These figures document target-level fusion performance. Establishing net electrical generation would additionally require facility-wide electrical measurements.

ITER’s FAQ defines plasma gain through the relationship between fusion power and external plasma heating. It describes ITER as an experimental device whose design excludes steam-generation and electricity-generation systems. Its intended contribution is experimental knowledge relevant to future fusion electricity plants. Statements about ITER’s design and gain definitions describe the experiment’s scope, and any future performance targets remain distinct from achieved operation.

The supplied review identifies some broader ITER FAQ language about burning plasma as overbroad when considered alongside LLNL’s inertial-fusion results. That limits the usefulness of those general statements for comparing achievements across fusion approaches. The specific descriptions of ITER’s design and energy-accounting definitions remain usable for the distinctions presented here.

Evidence scope. This record relies on the supplied review’s account of the retained sources. It reports complete, untruncated extractions of both pages with no extraction issues. Both are living pages retrieved on November 11, 2026, after the November 1, 2026 research cutoff, and the supplied bounded freshness-search record is empty. The explicitly dated June 2026 result can be retained, while the latest worldwide developments at the cutoff remain unverified. This limitation also leaves open whether another system had demonstrated the complete proposed capability.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration. Operate an integrated plant for a substantial campaign and show positive net electrical energy over the entire campaign, together with repeated positive operating intervals. Report gross electrical generation and all facility electrical consumption, including startup and shutdown. Define the measurement boundary so that internal loads are counted once. Where grid exports and imports provide the boundary measurement, use their net balance consistently. ITER’s whole-facility distinction motivates this proposal, while the acceptance criteria remain proposed.
completion_criteria.label: Positive net electrical energy across the entire integrated plant campaign

completion_criteria.text: Proposed test specification. Declare campaign duration, required availability, operating intervals and measurement uncertainty before testing. Include interruptions and recovery periods in the campaign account, and report both the total energy balance and the distribution of performance over time. The supplied material provides no consensus numerical threshold for campaign duration, availability or electrical surplus.
completion_criteria.label: Predeclared campaign criteria and complete energy performance reporting over time

completion_criteria.text: Proposed operational demonstration. Document component condition, maintenance interventions, replacement requirements and the plant’s return to productive operation. Establish a credible continuing fuel supply. For a deuterium–tritium plant, demonstrate integrated breeding, recovery and delivery of usable tritium sufficient for continued operation, with transparent inventory and flow accounting. The supplied sources leave the feasibility and appropriate quantitative acceptance thresholds for this fuel-cycle demonstration unresolved.
completion_criteria.label: Demonstrated maintenance recovery and sufficient continuing fuel supply

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility and practical boundaries. Make measurement methods, calibration, uncertainties, operating conditions and energy accounts available for independent assessment. Repeat the result across campaigns to establish reproducibility, and use additional plants to investigate replication. Any finite demonstration establishes performance within tested durations and conditions. Competitive lifecycle cost, manufacturing scale and reliable operation across a broader range of conditions would each require further evidence.
completion_criteria.label: Independently assessable measurements and reproducible campaigns within stated limits

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis. NUC-07, “Net-electric fusion using a low-neutron fuel cycle,” overlaps directly with the electricity-producing goal of NUC-01 and adds a fuel-cycle-specific requirement concerning neutron production. NUC-01 covers the integrated plant capability across fusion approaches. A successful implementation could satisfy both entries if it also met NUC-07’s low-neutron requirement.

Roster-based synthesis. NUC-06, “Reactor structural materials that remain reliable under extreme neutron exposure,” could contribute to fusion component durability where neutron exposure is significant. NUC-11, “Durable materials and chemistry control for aggressive reactor coolants,” could contribute where the selected heat-removal system creates demanding chemical conditions. These entries concern enabling capabilities that would require integration with fusion production, electricity conversion and fuel management to support NUC-01.

Roster-based synthesis. NUC-02, “Mass-produced fission plants with radically lower delivered cost,” shares the broader objective of practical nuclear electricity and the challenges of manufacturing, reliability and cost. Its central advance concerns fission-plant delivery economics. NUC-01’s proposed first achievement is sustained plant-wide net electricity from fusion, with competitive cost and mass deployment requiring subsequent evidence.

Roster-based synthesis. NUC-03, “A scalable closed fuel cycle that consumes most long-lived actinides,” and NUC-13, “A fuel cycle with substantially stronger built-in proliferation resistance,” share an emphasis on integrated fuel management. Their objectives address actinide consumption and proliferation resistance respectively. NUC-01 requires continuing fuel availability, including breeding and recovery for the proposed deuterium–tritium implementation, and leaves those other fuel-cycle outcomes to separate demonstrations.

Roster-based synthesis. NUC-05, “Practical remote verification of otherwise inaccessible operating reactors,” and NUC-12, “Reliable, non-invasive, real-time three-dimensional reactor-core diagnosis,” concern observing and interpreting reactor operation. Such capabilities could support verification, control or maintenance when applicable to a fusion design. Their success criteria concern the information obtained about a reactor, while NUC-01 requires an integrated electrical and operational result.

Roster-based synthesis. NUC-08, “Broadly applicable passive shutdown and long-term reactor cooling,” addresses safety functions that would require assessment for each relevant fusion design. NUC-09, “Very-high-burnup fuel with robust fission-product retention,” addresses fission-fuel performance. Neither capability follows from demonstrating a fusion plant’s positive electrical balance, and each retains its own scope.

Roster-based synthesis. NUC-04, “High-power nuclear propulsion for routine deep-space missions,” and NUC-10, “Long-lived, low-intervention nuclear power for remote sites,” could share demands for durable components and sustained operation. Their application requirements add propulsion performance or remote-service endurance. NUC-01 establishes the underlying fusion-electricity capability without resolving suitability for either application.

unresolved_issues: Whether any system had demonstrated the complete integrated capability worldwide as of November 1, 2026 remains unverified.
The supplied evidence does not establish the severity, relative importance or current resolution status of neutron-damage management and integrated tritium breeding and recovery.
Campaign duration, availability, electrical-surplus margin, accounting boundaries and acceptable measurement uncertainty require operational definitions before a proposed test.
The feasibility and quantitative acceptance criteria for an integrated deuterium–tritium breeding and recovery demonstration remain unresolved.
The supplied freshness record cannot establish whether the June 20, 2026 NIF result was the latest relevant achievement at the research cutoff.

Some broad ITER FAQ statements about burning plasma require scope clarification alongside the supplied inertial-fusion result. The record uses the design and accounting statements identified as usable by the review.
Competitive lifecycle costs, replication, manufacturing scale and deployment effects remain matters for further evidence.

brief.title: A power plant fueled by joining atoms
possible: Homes and businesses could draw electricity from fusion, the joining of light atoms to release energy. A working plant would generate enough electricity to run itself and supply a surplus, while keeping its equipment serviceable and its fuel supply going.
why: This would add a source of sustained electricity. It would connect fusion reactions to the full job of running a power plant, including powering its own equipment.
Reliable, affordable plants could expand electricity supplies and help reduce emissions where they replace higher-emission generation.

sources.who: Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory and collaborators
sources.showed: A laser experiment released approximately 3.8 times the energy delivered to its fuel target.
sources.quote: LLNL researchers continue to repeat the ignition achievement with increasing yield and target gain.
sources.cited_for: Fusion experiments can release more energy than the lasers deliver to the target.
sources.not_established: Energy released at the target does not establish an electricity surplus across the whole facility.

sources.showed: ITER explains how comparing fusion power with fuel-heating power differs from counting electricity generated and consumed across a whole plant.
sources.cited_for: A power plant must cover all its electrical demands before it can supply a surplus.
sources.not_established: ITER's design and performance goals do not demonstrate sustained electricity production.

shown: Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory has repeatedly achieved fusion ignition, where reactions release more energy than the lasers deliver to the target. ITER is an experiment designed to study fusion conditions; it has no electricity-generation systems.
missing: A plant would have to sustain an electricity surplus while counting startup, shutdown and every electrical load.
Equipment would have to remain serviceable, with maintenance followed by a return to productive operation.
Plants using tritium, a form of hydrogen, would have to produce, recover and deliver enough usable fuel for continued operation.

milestones.label: An electricity surplus across a full operating campaign
milestones.explanation: A substantial operating campaign would have to deliver an overall electricity surplus and repeated surplus-producing intervals, counting every facility load. This would establish that the complete plant produces usable electricity.

milestones.label: Performance measured against rules set before testing
milestones.explanation: Test duration, required operating time and measurement uncertainty would have to be declared beforehand, with interruptions and recovery included in results over time. This would make sustained performance assessable.

milestones.label: Recovery after maintenance and a continuing fuel supply
milestones.explanation: A plant would have to return to production after maintenance and sustain its fuel supply, including producing, recovering and delivering tritium where needed. This would establish that productive operation can continue.

milestones.label: Repeated results open to independent assessment
milestones.explanation: Measurements would have to support independent assessment, with repeated campaigns and additional plants used to investigate replication. This would establish repeatability within tested conditions, while broader reliability needs further evidence.

uncertain: How long must a qualifying campaign last, how often must the plant run, and how large must its electricity surplus be?
How demanding will damage from fusion neutrons, particles released by the reactions, and a continuing tritium supply prove in operating plants?
Can successful plants achieve competitive lifetime costs and be manufactured at scale?
